newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil well offered, jet fuel traded.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil well offered, jet fuel traded.

text.p: Singapore oil products were steady on Monday along with a firm crude market, traders said.

But gas oil appeared shaky due to the emergence of several offers around $32.20-$32.20 a barrel for January lifting, with a bid seen at a higher level of at $32.40. The well-offered market prompted the swaps market to dip about 40 cents from morning levels to be offered at $31.70, but still higher from Friday's $31.20/$31.40.
But traders said that if IPE maintained its rally--IPE last traded up $4.00 a tonne--the Singapore gas oil market might rise again on Tuesday.

The market largely ignored India's purchase of 90,000 tonnes of 0.5 percent sulphur gas oil in its second tender for January delivery. The tender was awarded at $25.85-$25.88 a tonne over high of Meditarranean quotes c+f Kandla. Traders said this reflected a more competitive Mediterranean market after several months of high prices there. A European major sold 120,000 barrels of jet fuel at $33.35 a barrel for Jan 3-7 lifting fob, five cents over the last jet deal on Friday.
A Dutch trader sold a 50,000-barrel cargo of 95-octane unleaded gasoline at $1.25 per barrel over Singapore naphtha related quotes, fob lifting January 1-5 to a Japanese trader.
A major indicated an offer at a $2.00 premium. January paper was pffered down from $25.90 to $25.60.

Naphtha also firmed with crude but the naphtha crack was weakening as support was weak with buyers staying on the sideline. South Korean petrochemical firms said they planned to reduce spot purchases in February to four to five cargoes from up to 12 cargoes monthly, and instead nominate term cargoes which were prices later. Indian awarded three sell tenders with the end-Dec/early Jan cargoes heading to North Asia and issued three more sell tenders for January.
